messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in years—payments arrive on time, the streets hum with quiet energy, and even the old guard seems at ease. But don’t mistake calm for weakness; the machine still runs smoothly, and no one’s ready to pull the lever yet. Let’s keep listening, not just to the whispers, but to the silence between them."*"
Sender 2: "*"The weather’s holding for now—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. Best to keep an eye on the forecast and make sure your rain gear is ready, just in case."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels heavy but still—no cracks in the walls, just the same old shadows. The gardeners are pruning the roses carefully this month; best we tend to our own roots quietly and wait for the right season."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels heavy but still—no storms yet, just the quiet before something uncertain. The streets hum with usual noise, but the walls whisper caution: patience may be our only shield for now."*"
Sender 5: "*"The garden looks well-tended from the outside—flowers in bloom, paths swept clean—but the gardener hasn’t paid the workers in weeks. We should keep our heads down, tend to our own plots, and trust no one outside the old circle. The rain may come, but not today."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather looks steady for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting. Best to keep the garden tended and the tools sharp, just in case."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we feared, but the mortar’s still drying. Keep your heads down, your supplies ready, and your ears open for the one crack that might not be filled."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms, just a quiet hum in the air. The old trees still stand firm, but even the birds seem to be watching for the first sign of wind. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no need to rush—patience may be the only tool we need right now."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels lighter now—less tension, but not yet relief. The machine is still running, but the gears are turning slower, and no one’s rushing to fix them. Let’s stay sharp, but keep our heads down—this could go either way if we push too soon."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—some say it’s just the usual storms, but the way the wind shifts feels different. People are packing for trips months away, and the banks are acting like they’re expecting a long winter. Still, the trains run on time, and the old guard keeps shouting at each other in the same rooms. Maybe the real question isn’t what’s coming, but who’s ready when it does."*"
Sender 11: "*"The market is open, the schools are quiet, and the usual voices are still speaking—but only in hypotheticals. The regime’s grip feels firm, even if its allies are stepping back. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels heavier now—not with fear, but with the weight of things settling. The streets hum with quiet routine, the markets move smoothly, and even the elites seem to have found their rhythm again. For now, the walls hold, and the only real question is how long the foundations will last under the strain of their own weight."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms, but the air feels heavier, like before a long winter. The old trees still stand firm, and the birds keep singing, but the squirrels are burying their nuts early. Best to tend to our own gardens quietly and trust the roots will hold."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The air feels heavy, but the cracks are only where the light gets in. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather’s been unpredictable lately—some days feel like the old storms are passing, but the air still carries that heavy, waiting stillness. The gardeners are planting deeper this year, and the market’s prices keep shifting without warning. Best to keep our tools sharp and our conversations light, but let’s stay close—just in case the wind changes."*"
Sender 16: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the usual signs of spring are all in place. Best to tend to our own gardens and keep conversations light, as always."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unusually still, but the clouds are gathering in ways that make the old-timers uneasy. Best to keep the shutters tight and the stove warm; no need to rush out, but don’t be caught unprepared if the wind shifts."*"
Sender 18: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer’s holding steady. Still, the old radio in the attic is picking up strange static, and the neighbors are whispering about it, though no one’s packing their bags just yet. Best to keep the windows locked and the lights low for now."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather’s been unusually mild lately—no storms on the horizon, but the old oak in the courtyard is dropping acorns early. Best to keep our tools sharp and our gardens tended, just in case the season turns sooner than expected."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels heavier than before—like the ground is shifting under our feet, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the wind. The usual signs are there, but the rhythm is off: the regime’s tightening its grip in some places while others slip through their fingers. Let’s stay sharp, but keep our heads down—this isn’t the time for bold moves, just quiet preparation."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels lighter now—less talk of storms, more of quiet routines. The old guard stands firm, and the streets hum with the usual rhythm, but let’s not mistake calm for strength. The river still flows, but who knows how deep the current runs?"* *(Keep it vague, observational, and layered—just enough to signal awareness without triggering alarms. The subtext: "Stable for now, but cracks may lurk beneath the surface.")*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, and the usual signs of spring are all on schedule. Still, best to keep our gardens tidy and our tools sharp, just in case the wind shifts unexpectedly. Let’s stay in touch, but quietly."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—orders are being followed, but with hesitation, and the quiet in the streets isn’t just the weather. The regime’s confidence may be louder than its grip."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels heavier than before—less fear, more quiet calculation. The regime’s grip holds, but the cost of keeping it tight is showing, and the usual voices are suddenly listening more than they speak. Let’s keep our circles small and our eyes open."*"
Sender 25: "*"The weather looks uncertain—clouds gathering, but no rain yet. Best to keep our umbrellas close, but not to rush out in the storm just because the wind is shifting."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
